display.purpose: One per surface. Ceiling derived from the longest line against the five-column measure; leading 1.0 clears the comma-below on Ț/Ș.

count.purpose: The category figure, pushed to the top of its cell. The number is the content; the name beneath it is the caption.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the featured unit name.

measurement.purpose: Headline prices and the catalog readout. Tabular figures, tracking zeroed.

measurement-compact.purpose: The price inside a catalog unit cell, where four cells share a row.

subhead.purpose: The supporting line under a display headline or inside a band, capped at 68ch, set in ink-soft.

title.purpose: The unit name inside a catalog cell.

body.purpose: Running text in cells and the footer.

note.purpose: Secondary running prose: qualifiers, step references, lending disclaimers. Sentence case, never tracked, never uppercase. Prose never uses label type.

label.purpose: Field names, nav items, grade names, financing tag. 0.75rem is the floor, raised from 0.6875rem after a legibility finding. Never a sentence, never a kicker above a heading.

fonts.note: latin-ext is mandatory: it carries ă Ă ș Ș ț Ț. Without it Romanian diacritics fall back to a system face mid-word.

materials.name: ink-field
materials.purpose: The only figure/ground shift. Bleeds to cell edges by negative gutter margins. The mechanism that makes cyan legible.

materials.name: screen-50
materials.purpose: Densest offset screen: the most visible wear on a grade plate.

materials.name: screen-05
materials.purpose: Lightest offset screen: no visible wear. Density is semantic, not texture.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Every state transition and the grid travel use it.

motion.name: duration-control
motion.purpose: Button background and colour inversion on hover.

motion.name: duration-link
motion.purpose: Nav item colour shift and filter button fill.

motion.name: duration-row
motion.purpose: Index row, catalog unit and category cell background fill on hover; grade fill opacity.

motion.name: duration-arrow
motion.purpose: Row and cell arrow translate of 0.25rem.

motion.name: duration-travel
motion.purpose: The catalog grid's FLIP travel, run through the Web Animations API against a geometry snapshot taken at the end of each layout effect. Surviving cells translate from their old offset to zero; they never crossfade. Cells moving under 1px are skipped, and prefers-reduced-motion skips the travel entirely. Also declared on the condition-axis fill transform, which is static per row and does not animate.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all CSS transitions and animations collapsed to 0.01ms; scripted travel gated on the same query
motion.purpose: Global prefers-reduced-motion honour, required by PRODUCT.md.

rules-primitives.name: rule
rules-primitives.purpose: Every ordinary boundary: cell dividers, row separators, band edges, catalog cell edges.

rules-primitives.name: rule-strong
rules-primitives.purpose: Terminal edge of a major region, the secondary button border, the filter bar frame and its internal divisions, the trust field's opening rule.

rules-primitives.name: gutter
rules-primitives.purpose: Cell padding and the negative margin that bleeds inverted fields to the cell edge.

rules-primitives.name: spans
rules-primitives.purpose: Placement on the shared twelve-column module. All collapse to span 12 below 1100px.

narrative.overview:
MYO is built as a Swiss International Style poster pasted flat on paper. One twelve-column module disciplines every surface; hairline navy rules, not boxes or shadows, build every boundary. Hierarchy comes from scale contrast and from where a thing sits on the grid, never from decoration. The surface is meant to read as an instrument: a seller who thinks in systems, grading hardware as measured records rather than selling it with badges.

The palette is a paper ground with navy ink and one violet signal that owns whole modules instead of scattering as accents. Two colours are held under strict conditions: cyan belongs only inside an inverted ink field and only to express condition; amber belongs only to financing, and only as a fill. Imagery is authored geometry — a quarter-arc, a bar ladder and dot screens drawn in brand colour — because the world is flat matte paper. Confirmed rejections, made when liquid-glass-js was dropped from the stack: no blur, no translucency, no specular glass, no soft gradient wash, no drop shadow, no rounded card.

Density is high and deliberately unpadded: cells are separated by rules rather than by whitespace, and type sizes are few and far apart. The system moves in one way only — the grid re-sorts and its cells travel to their new positions. Nothing crossfades, nothing lifts. Romanian is the primary market, so diacritics are a typographic constraint of the system, not a localisation afterthought.
keyCharacteristics: One twelve-column module, reused on every page including the 404
Hairline rules as the only boundary device; zero shadows, zero radii
Paper-white ground, navy ink, a single violet signal
Three materials only: paper, inverted ink field, offset dot screen
Two conditional colours (cyan for condition, amber for financing) under hard placement rules
Authored geometry as the only imagery; the geometry derives its length from the data
Motion is travel on the grid, never a fade
Browser chrome themed: selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring, underline offset

rules.name: The Contrast-Step Rule
rules.body: Violet has two steps and they are not interchangeable. #9B5DE5 may be display type, a fill or a rule; the moment violet carries reading text, a link or an icon, it becomes #6D28D9. Audit test: no text under 2.25rem is ever #9B5DE5.

rules.name: The Cyan-Never-On-Paper Rule
rules.body: Cyan appears only inside an ink field, and only to express condition or the wordmark. Three placements are sanctioned: mark field, condition ladder, unit grade chip. A fourth is added only by adding a fourth ink field — cyan on paper is a contrast failure (2:1), not a style choice.

rules.name: The Amber-Is-Fill-Only Rule
rules.body: Amber means financing and nothing else, and it is always a background with ink on top. Amber text does not exist in this system.

rules.name: The Screen-Density Rule
rules.body: The offset dot screen carries information, not texture. Three densities exist — 5px, 9px and 16px pitch — and the density is semantic: the heavier the screen, the more visible the wear it describes. A screen is never applied to make an empty area look designed, and no fourth density is invented without a fourth thing to mean.

rules.name: The Twelve-Px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text in this system is set below 0.75rem (12px). That is the floor for label type and it is a floor, not a target — it was raised from 0.6875rem after a legibility finding and must not be walked back for density.

rules.name: The Label-Is-Not-Prose Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase label type names a field in one or two words. Running prose never uses it. When prose must recede, it uses Note (0.875rem, sentence case, ink-muted). Audit test: no .label in the build contains a full sentence.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No tracked uppercase label may sit as its own block directly above a heading. A kicker was shipped and removed; the replacement is not a smaller kicker. Sequence, category and context belong in running text, in the heading itself, or in a field/value pair where the value follows the label.

rules.name: The Latin-Ext Rule
rules.body: Archivo is self-hosted through the Bunny provider with subsets latin and latin-ext. This is a hard requirement, not an optimisation: without latin-ext, Romanian ă/ș/ț fall back to a system face mid-word. Any font added to this project ships both subsets or is not added.

rules.name: The Longest-Line Rule
rules.body: The display ceiling is set by the longest word measured against its five-column column, not by taste. The current 5rem cap is what "INTELIGENT." (11 caps) allows; change the copy and the cap is re-derived, not guessed.

rules.name: The Comma-Below Rule
rules.body: Display leading is exactly 1.0 and must clear the descending comma on Ț and Ș against the next cap line. Any tighter leading collides with Romanian diacritics.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Every price, capacity and count carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums with tracking zeroed. Figures are measurements and must not shimmer between rows.

rules.name: The One Module Rule
rules.body: Every surface — homepage, placeholder pages, the 404 — is laid on the same twelve-column module. A new region picks a span utility; it does not invent a layout. A nested grid is allowed only when its columns divide the parent span evenly.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Boundaries are rules (1px ink at 22% for hairlines, solid ink for terminal edges), never borders used as decoration and never a box drawn around content for emphasis.

rules.name: The Travel-Not-Fade Rule
rules.body: When a control re-lays a grid, the surviving cells travel to their new positions — FLIP against a geometry snapshot, 420ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) — so the module is visibly the instrument doing the sorting. Cells do not crossfade, do not stagger in, and are not remounted. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the travel is skipped entirely and the new layout is simply there.

rules.name: The Zero-Shadow Rule
rules.body: box-shadow does not appear in this system. Not ambient, not on hover, not on focus, not as a hairline substitute. State is expressed by colour inversion, background fill and a 0.25rem translate, never by lift.

rules.name: The Inverted-Field Rule
rules.body: When a component needs to stand apart from the paper, it becomes an ink field bleeding to its cell edges — not a card, not a tint, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Three-Materials Rule
rules.body: Paper, ink field, offset screen. A new surface treatment is one of those three or it does not ship. There is no tint layer, no scrim, no frosted panel.

rules.name: The Square-Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is zero everywhere. A rounded card in this world reads as a foreign component, not a variant.

rules.name: The Authored-Geometry Rule
rules.body: Imagery is geometry this project draws: arcs, bars, rules, ladders, screens. No stock photography furniture, no gradient mesh, no glass. Product photography, when the catalog needs it, enters as a squared, full-bleed plate inside a cell — never as a floating rounded thumbnail.

rules.name: The Vocabulary-Length Rule
rules.body: Geometry that counts something takes the count as a parameter. The condition vocabulary is three steps — Bun, Excelent, Ca nou — and the mark, the ladder fill fractions and the axis note all derive from that length. Add or remove a grade and the drawing follows; no component carries a literal step count.

dos: Do lay every new surface on the twelve-column module with hairline-ruled cells, a span utility and the fluid clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2.5rem) gutter.
Do step violet down to signal-deep the moment it carries text, a link or an icon.
Do put cyan inside an ink field and nowhere else, and reserve it for condition and the wordmark.
Do keep label type at or above 0.75rem, in one or two words, naming a field.
Do use note (0.875rem, sentence case, ink-muted) whenever prose must recede.
Do ship every typeface with the latin-ext subset so Romanian diacritics render in the intended face.
Do set every price, capacity and count in tabular figures.
Do make a filtered grid travel: FLIP its surviving cells 420ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), and skip the travel under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do hold one piece of selection state per concept and pass it to every control that expresses it, so two surfaces can never disagree.
Do derive counted geometry from the data — the condition vocabulary is three steps and the drawing follows it.
Do let dot-screen density mean something: heavier screen, more visible wear.
Do express state by inversion, fill and small translate: 160–420ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
Do keep the 1100px collapse to full-width bands, and add a narrower breakpoint only to step down a nested grid's column count.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow anywhere, in any state, including as a fake hairline.
Don't round a corner; radius is 0 across the system.
Don't set body text, links or icons in signal violet, and never place cyan on paper.
Don't use amber as ink; it is a fill with ink on top or it is absent.

Don't introduce blur, translucency, specular glass or a soft gradient wash — they were rejected with the glass library when this world was chosen. The offset screen's radial-gradient is a hard-stopped dot grid, not a ramp, and is the only gradient function in the system.
Don't use a glyph icon font or an icon package; icons are inline SVG drawn in this vocabulary.
Don't set an uppercase label above a headline as a kicker or eyebrow. Labels name a field beside or beneath content, or pair with a value that follows them.
Don't set text below 0.75rem, and don't set a sentence in tracked uppercase.
Don't crossfade, stagger or remount a filtered list; the cells travel or nothing moves.
Don't let two controls for the same concept own separate state.
Don't apply a dot screen as decorative texture on an area that means nothing.
Don't wrap content in a card to group it; group it with a rule or an inverted field.
Don't centre a container or introduce a second grid; the module is full-bleed and singular.
